clue.text: Total rubbish cut back

indicators.note: back says the shortened word is then read from right to left
cut means the word for rubbish loses its final letter

parts.note: mush is soft pulpy stuff, nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A complaint that the entire amount of waste has been reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks MUSH to MUS, and 'back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the overall amount when figures are added together, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Turning over locations among irises to contain last of daffodils is wrong

indicators.note: turning over means flipping, so the whole assembly is read backwards
to contain means to hold inside, so the next letter goes within

parts.note: pupils are the dark openings set in the middle of the iris of each eye

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of daffodils

explanation.surface: Reads like gardening: bulbs among irises with daffodils planted in, then a verdict that it is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irises' sounds like flowers but means the eye; 'to contain' puts S in PUPILS and 'Turning over' reverses PUSPILS.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip up is to make a mistake, so it means to err.

clue.text: Middle of common containing lines for electronic device

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the next piece goes between those letters
the middle of the word means its central letters

parts.note: an ode is a poem, a few lines of verse

explanation.surface: Something ordinary holding wires, like a gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of' takes the two central letters of 'common'; 'containing' wraps them round the poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem links a computer to a network, a piece of electronic hardware.

clue.text: Democrat and Republican support receding — America's moment to interpose good candidates

indicators.note: to interpose is to come between, so these letters are placed inside the reversed support
receding means the word for support goes backwards

parts.note: a tee is the little peg that supports a golf ball
a tick is a very short moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: A political story: two US parties withdraw backing just as America picks fine runners for office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receding' reverses the golf support to EET; 'to interpose' sets the America and moment pieces inside it, after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream ticket is an ideal pairing of running mates, so the phrase describes outstanding candidates.

clue.text: Last month's speaker, one offering elaboration?

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the last month of the year
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: Last month's speaker is someone given to embellishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last month' wants to mean the month before this one; it is the year's final month.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorator adds ornament, so in a playful sense they elaborate on surfaces.

clue.text: Soccer team in upset promoted chemical preparation

indicators.note: in means placed inside the reversed word
promoted means raised up, so in this down entry the word reads upwards

parts.note: to rile is to upset or annoy
XI, eleven, is the number in a football side

explanation.surface: A football side, angered and then going up a division, with a potion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' turns RILE to ELIR in this down light, and XI goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a medicinal solution or potion, the alchemists' magic preparation.

clue.text: Items dished up with a lot of peas?

definitions.text: Items dished up with a lot of peas?

indicators.note: dished up means served out in a new arrangement, so these letters are shuffled
a lot of means most of the word, its last letter going

explanation.surface: Things served with plenty of peas, which is how pub pies come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' takes PEA from peas, and 'dished up' shuffles it with ITEMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pies filled with meat are classic British fare often served with mushy peas.

clue.text: Outcome is sequence of pieces lacking that certain something

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the following letters are removed

parts.note: a suite is a set of musical pieces played in order
it means an indefinable special quality, as in 'she has it'

explanation.surface: Talk of an end result that lacks a special spark.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is 'that certain something', the elusive quality.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue can mean a result or consequence, as in 'the issue of the debate'.

clue.text: Take no thanks, upset about following commotion

indicators.note: no says the letters for thanks are dropped

parts.note: ta is an informal British thank-you

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for upset surrounds the next letter

parts.note: to ruffle is to upset or disturb

explanation.surface: An instruction to grab without gratitude, upset over what followed the fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' drops the British slang thanks from 'Take', leaving KE; 'about' wraps the upset word round F.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerfuffle is a fuss or disturbance, a lively British word for a commotion.

clue.text: Murdoch's novel report about Biblical book

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for report surrounds the next piece

parts.note: to tell is to report or relate
Heb is the abbreviation for Hebrews, a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A media mogul's book reviewed alongside scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murdoch' suggests Rupert, the press baron, but is Iris Murdoch, the novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bell is Iris Murdoch's 1958 novel set in a lay religious community.

clue.text: Popular party attended by friend in Far Eastern locale

indicators.note: attended by means accompanied, so the next piece comes along after

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a do is a party or celebration
china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, from 'china plate'

explanation.surface: A well-liked party with a friend at it, set somewhere in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA for friend is Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with 'mate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Indochina is the old name for the peninsula of Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia, a region of Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Yes, I will set about Government upturn

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the agreement word encloses the next letter

parts.note: 'Sure!' is a casual way of saying 'yes, I will'

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to tackle a government's sudden improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' looks like 'begin', but here it means put around.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden rise, as in a surge in sales, so it matches an upturn.

clue.text: Warrior spirit recalled in South America — excellent

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for spirit is read backwards

parts.note: rum is a distilled spirit
A1 means first-rate, read here as the letters AI

explanation.surface: A fighter's courage remembered in South America is first-class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns RUM into MUR; 'excellent' is A1, with the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the hereditary military class of feudal Japan, so the word names a type of warrior.

clue.text: Pair to get away from for a start

definitions.note: here a noun, the opening piece of something

parts.note: to elude is to escape from or evade

explanation.surface: Two people trying to escape, for a start.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelude is an introductory piece or event that comes first, so it is a beginning.

clue.text: Fairly narrow-minded about rule

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for narrow-minded wraps the next letter

parts.note: petty means small-minded or narrow-minded

explanation.surface: A judgement that someone is somewhat bigoted when it comes to regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, pretty means moderately, as in 'pretty good', so it matches fairly.

clue.text: A lot of death sentences, after first three, commuted to life

indicators.note: a lot of means most, so the last letter goes

parts.note: exit is a euphemism for death, a departure from life

indicators.note: commuted means changed, so the remaining letters are rearranged
after first three means the opening three letters are dropped

explanation.surface: Many capital sentences commuted to life imprisonment, a legal story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' docks the last letter of the death word; 'after first three' leaves TENCES for 'commuted' to shuffle. 'commuted' plays on a reduced prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence is the state of being alive, a synonym for life.

clue.text: Perhaps refraining from striking head of match (variety of lucifer)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so the opening letter of match is taken
a variety of the word is a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A lucifer was a kind of match, so the clue reads like a note on match types and their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges LUCIFER into ERCIFUL. 'Striking' pretends to be about matches; in the definition it means hitting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding back from hitting someone is an example of showing compassion, hence the 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Niger unexpectedly invading another African country was vexing

definitions.note: past-tense verb sense: was vexing means was annoying someone, i.e. made them cross

indicators.note: invading means getting inside, so the rearranged letters go into the country

parts.note: Chad is a country in central Africa

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests a surprise turn, so the letters of Niger are rearranged

explanation.surface: An African state invades its neighbour, which is troubling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges NIGER to GRINE, which goes 'invading' CHAD. Niger and Chad are neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: To chagrin is to annoy or mortify someone, so having done so is having been irritating.

clue.text: Raised flageolet, note, during country dance — it's revelatory

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, so in this down entry the word reads upwards

parts.note: a flageolet is a small flute, a type of pipe

indicators.note: during means within, so the note letter goes inside the dance

parts.note: the hay is an old English country dance with weaving figures

explanation.surface: A flute held aloft, a note sounding mid-dance at a folk gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns the flute word upwards to EPIP; 'during' sets the note within the old dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An epiphany is a sudden moment of insight, a revelation.

clue.text: Opening comment, say, about page 1: 'Page enveloped in cheer'

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters for say surround the next pieces

parts.note: e.g. means 'for example', a sense of 'say'
the figure 1 resembles the letter I

indicators.note: enveloped in means wrapped inside, so the letter for page goes within the cheer

parts.note: rah is a shout of cheer, short for hurrah

explanation.surface: Looks like an editor's note about a quotation on page 1 involving a cheerful page boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'enveloped in' are both containers. The colon and quotation marks are only dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigraph is a short quotation set at the start of a book or chapter, hence an introductory remark.

clue.text: Gradually develops volume that's brought in days before

indicators.note: brought in means put inside, so the volume letters go within the days

parts.note: eves are the days before festivals, as in Christmas Eve

explanation.surface: A book that gets delivered the previous day slowly takes shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' places the volume abbreviation after the first letter of the days.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to change slowly over time, a synonym for unfolding by degrees.

clue.text: Various names including English and Asian name

indicators.note: including means containing, so the next letter goes inside the rearranged letters
various suggests different arrangements, so the letters of names are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of different names takes in both English and Asian ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges NAMES and 'including' adds E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Naseem is a given name of Arabic origin used across South Asia, as borne by the boxer Prince Naseem Hamed.

clue.text: Vehicle climbing in distance makes you wonder

definitions.note: a phrase defining a noun: something that astonishes

indicators.note: in means inside the word for distance

parts.note: a mile is a distance

indicators.note: climbing means going up, so in this down entry the word reads upwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car going up into the distance is an astonishing sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns CAR to RAC, which goes 'in' MILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A miracle is an extraordinary event that causes astonishment, a source of wonder.

clue.text: Demolition of tree occurring in very sound system

indicators.note: occurring in means happening inside, so the shuffled letters go within

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'

indicators.note: demolition means knocking down, so the letters of tree are rearranged

explanation.surface: Felling a tree in a very healthy state, sound in the sense of solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demolition of' rearranges the tree to TERE, which goes 'occurring in' the word for very. 'Sound' looks like 'healthy' but is audio.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo is a hi-fi set that plays music, an audio system.

clue.text: Sudden appearance that's no longer raised?

parts.note: out means finished or over, no longer in play
a crop is something raised, as farmers raise crops

explanation.surface: A question about something once cultivated but no longer grown.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is something that comes into view, as rock breaking through the soil, so it is an emergence.

clue.text: Some Italian men upset Italian city, putting out Italian article

definitions.note: adjective in the answer, describing some Italian men, those from the capital

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the remaining letters are rearranged
putting out means removing, so the article letter is taken away

parts.note: Marino is a town in the Alban Hills just south-east of Rome
i is the Italian plural article, 'the'

explanation.surface: Some Italian men disturb a city in Italy by ejecting a grammatical word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting out' drops I from MARINO to leave MARNO, and 'upset' shuffles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Men from Italy's capital are described by this adjective, a subset of Italians.

clue.text: Crude routine holding force back in struggle for territory

indicators.note: back says the whole assembly is read from right to left
holding means keeping between, so the force letter sits between the two words

parts.note: raw means crude or unrefined
a rut is a dull fixed routine
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: A rough drill with force behind it, as in a fight over land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' sets the force letter between the crude and routine words; 'back' reverses all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A turf war is a dispute between gangs or departments over who controls an area, a fight over ground.

clue.text: About half the population currently upset about the writer

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed word surrounds the next piece
upset means turned upside down, so in this down entry the word reads upwards

parts.note: now means currently, at present
the writer refers to the setter, ME

explanation.surface: Half of all people are currently troubled about the author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses NOW to WON, which goes 'about' ME. The first 'About' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughly half of humanity is female, so the adult females make up about half.

clue.text: Married individual against returning spiteful talk

indicators.note: returning means the assembled letters are read backwards

parts.note: one means a single individual
V is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A married person, coming back, is against nasty gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses MONEV.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is figuratively bitter malice in speech, so it covers vicious words.

clue.text: Way of working recalled in development of organic farmer's market may be so described

definitions.text: farmer's market may be so described

indicators.note: in means placed inside the rearranged word
a development of the word is a reworking of its letters
recalled means called back, so the letters for way of working are reversed

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: A habit being recalled while an organic farmers' market grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns MO into OM, which goes 'in' AGRONIC, the rearrangement of ORGANIC from 'development of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agronomic means relating to the science of crop production, a fitting description of a farming business.

clue.text: Barber went crazy, with odd eyes

indicators.note: crazy means wild or disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hairdresser loses his mind and develops strange eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges WENT, ODD and EYES together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeney Todd is the murderous fictional barber of Fleet Street, the 'Demon Barber' of Victorian melodrama.

clue.text: Born poet's still back-pedalling

indicators.note: back-pedalling suggests going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: e'en is the poetic contraction of even, meaning still

explanation.surface: A born poet is still backtracking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-pedalling' turns E'EN round.
explanation.definitionFit: Née, French for born, introduces a married woman's maiden name, as in 'Mrs Smith, née Jones'.
